channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: Os três deputados barrados por Moraes de visitar Filipe Martins
item.description: Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes barred three federal deputies — Gustavo Gayer (PL), Marcel Van Hattem (Novo), and Carlos Jordy (PL) — from visiting Filipe Martins, former aide to Jair Bolsonaro, who is serving a 21-year sentence for his role in a coup plot. Moraes denied access because the deputies are under investigation by the STF in connection with the same criminal case. While 14 other lawmakers were permitted to visit, these three were blocked due to their alleged ties to anti-democratic acts, criticism of federal police officials, and involvement in investigations related to the January 8 attacks.

item.title: Com quem será?
item.description: The dispute for a majority in Brazil's Supreme Federal Court (STF) is intensifying as Minister Luis Fux is expected to leave the First Chamber, paving the way for Lula's nominee for Chief of Staff, Jorge Messias, to join the bloc — despite receiving support from Bolsonaro-appointed ministers like André Mendonça and Nunes Marques, as well as government allies such as Gilmar Mendes. The article highlights that this articulation unfolds amid an institutional crisis at the STF, where previously covert maneuvers are becoming overt in the struggle to control the majority of the plenary or the First Chamber.

item.title: Avançou o projeto que pode proibir entrada de Moraes nos EUA, mas sua votação é incerta
item.description: The 'No Censors on Our Soil' bill has advanced to a vote in the U.S. House of Representatives and could bar entry or lead to deportation of individuals deemed foreign agents who censure American citizens, potentially including Brazilian Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes. However, its passage remains uncertain due to partisan divisions and constitutional concerns.

item.title: Na caça ao líder Palmeiras, Fluminense e Flamengo fazem clássico no Maracanã após adiamento polêmico
item.description: Fluminense and Flamengo face off today at 6 PM at Maracanã in the 11th round of the Brasileirão, after the match was postponed due to Flamengo’s delayed return from Peru. Both teams are fighting to stay in the Libertadores qualification zone, with Fluminense in third (20 points) and Flamengo in fifth (17 points), behind league leaders Palmeiras (25 points). Flamengo arrives on a two-match winning streak and will field its starters, while Fluminense aims to improve finishing after two recent setbacks.

item.title: Diante do avanço de Flávio, Lula endurece discurso sobre segurança
item.description: President Lula is hardening his security discourse in response to Flávio Bolsonaro's rise in polls, aiming to attract center-leaning voters concerned about violence. He has adopted a punitive tone, calling for imprisoning criminals, increasing penalties for gender-based violence offenders, and targeting phone theft, seeking to counter the left's perceived leniency on crime. This shift is seen as a test to reposition the PT ahead of the 2026 election.

item.title: No centro de disputa global, terras-raras viram pauta de pré-candidatos a presidente
item.description: Rare earth elements have become a strategic issue in Brazil's 2026 presidential pre-campaigns, with opposition candidates like Flávio Bolsonaro, Romeu Zema, and Ronaldo Caiado seeking electoral gains by aligning with the Trump administration's goal of reducing dependence on Chinese rare earths. President Lula maintains a sovereignty-focused narrative, while analysts note the topic blends domestic politics and foreign relations, particularly given the interventionist posture of the U.S. government.

item.title: Disputa para governos e Senado tem baixa representatividade feminina e cenário repete pleitos anteriores
item.description: Female representation in pre-candidacies for state governorships and the Senate in 2026 remains low, repeating patterns from previous elections, with only 11 states having female gubernatorial candidates and few or none for the Senate in some cases. Despite rhetoric from candidates like Lula, Flávio Bolsonaro, and Ronaldo Caiado on gender violence and women-focused proposals, parties continue to favor men in majoritarian tickets, as the 30% female candidacy quota applies only to proportional races. Experts note the lack of legal obligation for executive offices, combined with male-dominated party leadership, perpetuates underrepresentation.

item.title: Indecisos afirmam que caso Master impacta voto e se dividem sobre campo que sofreu o maior baque
item.description: Undecided voters in the 2026 Brazilian presidential election say the Master case will influence their vote, though they disagree on which political sphere was most affected by the scandal. While split between left and right, they also diverge on the impact of Lula’s government measures to recover popularity, but agree that a third-way right-wing option would be preferable to Flávio Bolsonaro’s candidacy, which faces resistance in this group.

item.title: Não existe alternativa ao ajuste fiscal
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva will leave the obligation to implement a fiscal adjustment as early as 2027 to his successor — whether himself or another — according to William Maloney, the World Bank’s chief economist for Latin America and the Caribbean. Maloney stated that any government taking office in January 2027 will need to focus on fiscal consolidation, as current palliative measures are unsustainable. The article is exclusive to subscribers of the originating outlet.

item.title: A armadilha que Lula pode ter criado para si mesmo na eleição
item.description: Lula expressed concern about televised debates in the 2026 election, questioning how many opposition candidates would participate and suggesting less formal formats, such as meetings with fewer rules or a 'mix-up'. He indicated a preference for more flexible debates, possibly to avoid structured confrontations that could disadvantage him. The comment reflects a strategy to control the narrative and limit exposure to direct challenges in high-visibility settings.

item.title: PT minimiza empate de Flávio e culpa INSS e Master pelo desgaste
item.description: PT leaders downplayed the technical tie between Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) and Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) in the runoff scenario, attributing Lula’s decline to scandals involving Banco Master, INSS fraud suspicions, and allegations against the president’s son, while emphasizing that investigations are being driven by Lula’s government. Edinho Silva and Lindbergh Farias framed the shift as a product of anti-system sentiment and expressed confidence in Lula’s re-election once formal campaigning begins and new economic measures take effect.

item.title: Lula tem 40% de avaliação negativa e 29% de positiva, diz pesquisa Datafolha
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva has a 40% negative and 29% positive approval rating according to a Datafolha poll, with overall disapproval stable at 51% and approval slightly down to 45%. In a hypothetical 2026 runoff, Lula is technically tied with Flávio Bolsonaro (45% to 46%), while leading by six points in the first round (38% to 32%). Both candidates show high rejection rates (Lula: 48%, Flávio: 46%), reflecting deep political polarization in Brazil.

item.title: Avaliação positiva do governo Lula piora em abril, mostra Datafolha
item.description: Positive evaluation of Lula's government dropped from 32% to 29% in April, while regular rose from 26% to 29% and negative remained at 40%. Approval of Lula's work fell from 47% to 45% and disapproval rose from 49% to 51%. In a potential runoff, Flávio Bolsonaro leads with 46% against Lula's 45%, within the margin of error.

item.title: Datafolha: governo Lula tem 40% de avaliação negativa e 29% de positiva
item.description: President Lula's government has a 40% negative rating (bad or terrible) and 29% positive rating (excellent or good), according to a Datafolha poll released on April 11. Negative approval remained stable since March, while positive approval dropped 3 percentage points and those rating the government as 'regular' rose to 29%. On approval, 51% disapprove (+2 p.p) and 45% approve (-2 p.p).

item.title: Sucesso da Artemis II distrai os EUA e o mundo, mas não esconde o ‘admirável mundo novo de Trump’
item.description: While Artemis II is celebrated as a historic success, it serves as a distraction from Donald Trump’s harmful actions against democracy, global stability, and human rights. His explicit threats of genocide against Iran reveal an authoritarian pattern met with no consequences, as U.S. institutions — judiciary, military, Congress — remain passive, allowing him to operate above the Constitution and common sense. This collective silence contrasts sharply with Brazil’s firm response to the 2022 coup attempts, revealing a systemic failure in defending American democracy.

item.title: Flávio volta a fazer dancinha no lançamento de Zucco no RS
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro performed his signature dance again at the event launching Luciano Zucco as the PL's pre-candidate for governor of Rio Grande do Sul in Porto Alegre. The move is part of a strategy to soften the public image of the Bolsonaro family. Zucco presented Bolsonaro with a symbolic letter containing RS's demands, focusing on state debt renegotiation, and confirmed the PP alliance, with Silvana Covatti expected as his running mate.

item.title: Mesmo que Bolsonaro filho evapore, Lula está perto de perder para um anti-Lula qualquer
item.description: Lula is at risk of losing the 2026 elections to an anti-Lula candidate, according to Datafolha data. If Ronaldo Caiado or Romeu Zema face him in a runoff, Lula would secure 45% of the vote against 42% for the opponent, showing an extremely tight race. Even if Bolsonaro’s influence fades, anti-Lula sentiment remains strong enough to defeat the incumbent president.

item.title: Delegado da PF é detido após tentar furtar vidro de carpaccio de trufa em shopping de Recife
item.description: Federal Police delegate Erick Blatt was detained after being caught on video stealing a luxury truffle carpaccio jar worth R$300 at a supermarket in Recife's RioMar Shopping. He paid for other items but concealed the truffle product, which was recovered by security at the exit. Blatt, former ADPF-RJ director who cleared Flávio Bolsonaro in an electoral falsehood investigation, gave testimony and is now under inquiry for theft.

item.title: Eduardo Bolsonaro fala em voltar ao Brasil caso Flávio seja eleito
item.description: Eduardo Bolsonaro stated he intends to return to Brazil if his brother, Flávio Bolsonaro, is elected president of the Republic. The remark was made in a video shown at a PL event in Porto Alegre, where he conditioned his return on Flávio's electoral outcome.

item.title: Flávio repete Eduardo e manda corda para prisão de enforcado
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro recorded a video defying the Supreme Court's digital silence order imposed on his father, Jair Bolsonaro, repeating a gesture previously made by his brother Eduardo. The video was intended to be viewed by Jair Bolsonaro at his residence, constituting a new affront to the authority of Justice Alexandre de Moraes. The action reflects the Bolsonaro family's continued defiance of judicial rulings, despite prior consequences.

item.title: BYD Qin L 2026 faz 36 km/l e já mira o Brasil
item.description: BYD unveiled the Qin L 2026, a plug-in hybrid sedan achieving 36 km/l, positioned above the King model with a focus on energy efficiency and cost-benefit. The vehicle combines an internal combustion engine with an electric motor to reduce fuel consumption and emissions, targeting both urban use and long-distance travel. BYD is expanding its plug-in hybrid lineup across price points and already has its sights set on the Brazilian market.

item.title: Rejeição de Lula chega a 48% e a de Flávio, 46%, diz Datafolha
item.description: Lula has 48% rejection and Flávio Bolsonaro 46%, according to a Datafolha poll from April 2026. In a potential runoff, Flávio leads Lula 46% to 45%, while Zema and Caiado show low rejection (17% and 16%) but limited name recognition. With a 2-point margin of error, all scenarios are statistically tied.

item.title: Fux vota para rever condenações de réus do 8 de janeiro
item.description: Supreme Court Minister Luiz Fux voted to overturn the convictions of ten defendants involved in the January 8, 2023 riots, now advocating for total or partial acquittals after initially supporting the majority’s condemnation. His shift has sparked debate over accountability criteria in the events.

item.title: A condenação do bolsonarista que depredou o gabinete de Janja no 8 de Janeiro
item.description: Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes declared the final and unappealable conviction of Vitorio Campos da Silva, a Bolsonarist dentist who vandalized the office of First Lady Janja during the January 8 attacks. He was sentenced to 14 years in prison for his role in the coup attempt, with the First Chamber of the STF rejecting his appeals on March 30 and the ruling certified on April 6. The PGR emphasized that his actions were not isolated but part of a sustained pattern of anti-democratic mobilization since 2020.

item.title: Datafolha esboça o embate da direita pelo posto de anti-Lula
item.description: The latest Datafolha poll shows that Lula's advantage in potential runoff scenarios has faded, indicating a weakening of his electoral position. Furthermore, Flávio Bolsonaro is no longer the sole competitive right-wing challenger, as other figures emerge as alternatives to Lula within the conservative camp.

item.title: Zema brinca em vídeo sobre convite para Flávio Bolsonaro ser seu vice
item.description: Romeu Zema (Novo) and Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) appeared in a lighthearted video in which Zema jokingly suggested the senator as his potential running mate for president. Posted on April 11, 2026, the clip shows the two toasting and laughing to a social media trend soundtrack, without any formal commitment. Bolsonaro has not yet announced his vice-presidential pick, though he previously mentioned Senator Tereza Cristina as his 'dream choice' for the role.

item.title: Série D ZeroUm: Metrópoles transmite jogo do Gama-DF x Inhumas-GO. Siga no YouTube
item.description: Gama-DF will face Inhumas-GO on Saturday (April 11) at 7:30 PM Brasília time at Bezerrão Stadium, in the 2nd round of Group A3 of the 2026 Série D. The match will be streamed live on Metrópoles Esportes' YouTube channel, which is broadcasting 20 matches per round throughout the 10-matchday second phase of Série D ZeroUm, with 10 games on Saturday and 10 on Sunday.

item.title: “Jair Bolsonaro vai subir a rampa junto com a gente”, diz Flávio
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro stated at an event in Rio Grande do Sul that, if elected president in 2026, he intends to walk up the ramp of the Palácio do Planalto alongside his father, former president Jair Bolsonaro. The remark was made during a speech tied to the launch of PL pre-candidacies in the state, reinforcing the narrative of familial continuity in power. Flávio emphasized that victory would represent not just a personal achievement, but a collective family project for Brazil.

item.title: Lindbergh minimiza pesquisa Datafolha e diz crer em reeleição de Lula
item.description: Deputy Lindbergh Farias (PT-RJ) downplayed the Datafolha poll showing Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) ahead of Lula (PT) at 46% to 45%, stating the numbers are a 'snapshot of the moment' and reaffirming confidence in Lula's re-election. He emphasized that the campaign has not yet begun and that truth will prevail over fake news when it starts. The result represents a technical tie within the two-point margin of error.

item.title: O papel de André Mendonça na campanha de Jorge Messias ao STF
item.description: With Jorge Messias' Senate hearing scheduled for April 29, André Mendonça, a Supreme Court justice, has played a key role in supporting the Lula administration's nominee, publicly praising Messias' work at the AGU and stating that 'ideology does not divide, character comes first'. Messias is optimistic about securing the necessary votes for approval in the CCJ and the full Senate.

item.title: Zema ‘convida’ Flávio Bolsonaro para ser vice em meio à especulação de possível chapa; veja vídeo
item.description: Romeu Zema (Novo) and Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) shared a joking video in which Zema 'invited' Bolsonaro to be his running mate, though both denied any formal discussion. Zema reiterated he will maintain his presidential pre-candidacy, while Bolsonaro is technically tied with Lula in a potential runoff, according to a Datafolha poll showing a slight edge for the Bolsonarist.

item.title: Bolsonaristas adotam 8 de Janeiro como plataforma eleitoral com filiações ao PL e ao Partido Novo
item.description: Bolsonarists are adopting January 8 as an electoral platform, with pre-candidates from PL and Novo Party advocating amnesty for the convicted and annulment of STF proceedings. Figures like Luiza Cunha ('Daughter of Clezão'), Carolina Siebra, and Cláudia Rodrigues are affiliating with parties to run for federal office, turning the event into a symbol of political and legal resistance.

item.title: Após racha em SP, Ciro Nogueira deve comandar federação União-Progressistas em SP
item.description: Ciro Nogueira, national president of the Progressistas party, is set to assume leadership of the União Brasil-Progressistas federation in São Paulo to resolve a power struggle between Maurício Neves (Progressistas) and Milton Leite (União Brasil). The decision, already approved by União Brasil’s national executive, includes transferring the Rio de Janeiro federation leadership to Antônio Rueda of União Brasil. The agreement aims to balance power, with each party controlling nine states.

item.title: Flávio diz que se vencer eleição, vai subir a rampa do Planalto acompanhado do pai Jair Bolsonaro
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro stated that if he wins the 2026 election, he will ascend the Planalto ramp at inauguration accompanied by his father, former President Jair Bolsonaro, who is currently under house arrest for his role in the coup plot. He also defended those convicted for the January 8 attacks and supported an amnesty bill in Congress that would benefit his father and others involved. A Datafolha poll shows Flávio at 46% and Lula at 45% in a hypothetical runoff, technically tied due to a 2-point margin of error.

item.title: Zema posta com Flávio e aumenta rumor de chapa conjunta
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) posted an Instagram video alongside former Minas Gerais governor Romeu Zema (Novo), joking about forming a 2026 presidential ticket, reversing prior pressure on Zema to step down from the top of the ticket. The post came hours after a Datafolha poll showed Bolsonaro tied with Lula in a potential runoff (46% to 45%) and Zema also statistically tied with the president. Social media users reacted enthusiastically to the prospect of an alliance between the two figures.

item.title: Pacote de combate ao endividamento pode virar arma eleitoral para estimular consumo
item.description: The Lula government is discussing debt-relief measures as a potential electoral tool to stimulate consumption, amid political pressure to lower high interest rates. The Selic rate remains at 14.75%, held by the Central Bank, sparking internal conflict between economic officials and allies advocating for looser monetary policy to boost the economy in an election year.

item.title: Lindbergh minimiza resultado do Datafolha e diz que campanha ainda nem começou
item.description: Lindbergh Farias, federal deputy from PT-RJ and vice-leader of the government in the Chamber of Deputies, downplayed the results of the Datafolha poll released on Saturday, the 11th, stating that the campaign for Lula’s re-election has not yet begun. He expressed confidence in President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva’s victory in the 2026 elections, despite the poll numbers.

item.title: Fux revê voto sobre 8/1 e absolve sete réus: ‘Injustiças que a consciência não me permite sustentar’
item.description: Supreme Court Justice Luiz Fux voted to overturn convictions of ten defendants in the January 8 attacks, fully acquitting seven and reducing sentences in three others, stating his prior vote was unjust and no longer sustainable by his conscience. The change is unlikely to alter practical outcomes, as only two other justices originally held this view.

item.title: Promotores reelegem Paulo Sérgio Costa chefe do Ministério Público de SP; escolha cabe a Tarcísio
item.description: Paulo Sérgio de Oliveira e Costa was re-elected as head of São Paulo’s Public Prosecutor’s Office with 1,305 votes, defeating his rival Marco Antônio Ferreira Lima. His reappointment depends on Governor Tarcísio de Freitas, who may select any candidate regardless of the election outcome. In his first term, he recovered R$4 billion in evaded taxes and strengthened the MP’s efforts against organized crime and corruption in the state treasury.

item.title: Em vídeo, Zema convida Flávio a compor chapa como vice
item.description: Former governor Romeu Zema jokingly suggested that Senator Flávio Bolsonaro could be his running mate in a potential presidential ticket. The video was posted by Flávio Bolsonaro on social media, showing the two pre-candidates toasting after the suggestion. The interaction was lighthearted, with no formal alliance confirmed.

item.title: Após Datafolha, Zema e Flávio Bolsonaro brincam sobre aliança: “Será?”
item.description: Romeu Zema and Flávio Bolsonaro joked in a video about a potential 2026 presidential alliance, hours after a Datafolha poll showed Flávio technically ahead of Lula in a runoff scenario. Despite the joke, Zema had previously rejected being vice president, saying he would run his candidacy to the end. The poll also showed Lula at 39% and Flávio at 35% in the first round, with Zema in fourth at 4%.

item.title: PSOL lança William Siri ao governo do Rio de Janeiro
item.description: The PSOL has formally launched the pre-candidacy of Rio de Janeiro city councilor William Siri for the state governorship in the October 2026 elections, ruling out a supplementary election. Siri denounced traditional political groups for decades of neglecting the state. Meanwhile, the STF is deliberating on an indirect election via the State Legislature, with voting paused after Minister Flávio Dino requested a view.

item.title: Pimenta assume liderança do governo na Câmara
item.description: Federal Deputy Paulo Pimenta (PT-RS) assumes the leadership of Lula's government in the Chamber of Deputies, replacing José Guimarães (PT-CE), who left the post to head the Secretariat of Institutional Relations. Pimenta previously served in Lula's administration, having headed the Presidency's Secretariat of Communication and worked in the Extraordinary Secretariat.

item.title: O acúmulo de críticas de Ratinho a questões políticas no SBT
item.description: SBT presenter Ratinho has intensified his criticism of the Lula government, addressing issues such as tax increases on medicines, Social Security management, INSS frauds, and Brazil's involvement in the Middle East conflict. He accused the government of lacking character, corruption, and exploiting citizens without delivering concrete benefits, prompting concern at the network over political content. His remarks, made live and on social media, reflect a populist and critical discourse toward the federal administration, particularly on economic and pension matters.

item.title: Gleisi diz que Guimarães fará articulação política com amplo respeito no Congresso
item.description: Federal deputy Gleisi Hoffmann (PT-PR) stated that deputy José Guimarães (PT-CE) will conduct political articulation with broad respect in Congress, commenting on his appointment to head the Secretariat of Institutional Relations (SRI). Gleisi emphasized that President Lula's nomination recognizes Guimarães' work in leading the government in the Chamber of Deputies and ensures dialogue commensurate with the nation's challenges. Guimarães will take office as minister next Tuesday, the 14th.

item.title: Governistas se preocupam com pesquisa que mostra Flávio numericamente à frente de Lula e veem influência de caso Master
item.description: Datafolha poll shows Lula at 45% and Flávio Bolsonaro at 46% in a simulated runoff, technically tied within the margin of error. Government allies attribute Lula’s decline to the fallout from the Master bank scandal, which involves payments to former ministers linked to both government and opposition, while insisting the poll is merely a 'snapshot' and the situation could change.

item.title: Flávio celebra Datafolha com empate técnico contra Lula
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro celebrated a technical tie with Lula in the April 2026 Datafolha poll, showing 46% to 45%, emphasizing the early stage of his presidential pre-campaign with informal language, personal references like 'father of a girl', and a less confrontational tone than his father’s. Deputy Lindbergh Farias (PT) maintained confidence that Lula will be re-elected, stating the campaign has not yet begun and that the government will reveal 'who is who' when it starts.

item.title: Hugo Motta diz que vê de forma positiva escolha de Guimarães para SRI
item.description: Chamber of Deputies President Hugo Motta praised President Lula's appointment of federal deputy José Guimarães (PT) to lead the Secretariat of Institutional Relations (SRI), calling it a positive development. The statement was made to Broadcast Político on Saturday, April 11.

item.title: O otimismo de Jorge Messias com a sabatina no Senado
item.description: Jorge Messias, Lula's nominee for the Supreme Court, expresses optimism ahead of his Senate confirmation hearing on April 29, noting growing support even among opposition senators. He says he is confident in his work at the AGU and pleased with the reception among lawmakers. Senate President Davi Alcolumbre forwarded the nomination to the CCJ, with Senator Weverton Rocha as rapporteur.

item.title: TSE deve publicar 2ª-feira acórdão sobre governo do Rio sem decisão sobre nova eleição
item.description: The TSE is set to publish on Monday, the 13th, the ruling that annulled the mandate of Rio de Janeiro Governor Cláudio Castro. The decision allows the STF to resume voting on how the next governor of the state will be chosen, without yet determining whether a new election will be held.
